newsitem.title: USA: Massport's BOSFUEL revenue bonds A3 by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Massport's BOSFUEL revenue bonds A3 by Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investor Service Friday rated A3 the initial $120 million special facilities revenue bonds for Massport's BOSFUEL project at Logan International Airport.

In its credit perspective statement, Moody's said the rating reflects the "joint and several obligation of the fuel users, the diversity of the airlines, the essentiallity of the system" to the airport's operation as well as the "limited revenue pledge, the lack of mortgage interest property being financed...and the obligation of BOSFUEL to finance future environmental remediation if necessary."

BOSFUEL is a Delaware Corp that was formed to fiannce and operate the fuel system at Logan and Massport, the airport's operator, has granted BOSFUEL a 42-year exclusive concession to distribute aviation fuel at the facility, Moody's noted.
BOSFUEL will consolidate the airport's existing fuel storage facilities, upgrade and consolidate the existing fuel distribution system and meet future aircraft fueling needs, Moody's said.

The contract's exclusivity provision is central to the A-level rating, Moody's noted. Lease payments from BOS FUEL are made to Massport, which then assigns and pledges the debt service payments to the trustee. An additional credit strength, Moody's said, was Massport's pledge to operate the facility for the benefit of the bondholders in the event of BOSFUEL's default.
But the rating agency cautioned, "this transaction is a special facilities financing and has no recourse to Massport for payment of debt service."
